title: Network election desk
notes: A documented global style guide now defines the game's 1976 network television art direction, typography, palette, motion, geometry, and accessibility rules.
The title screen remains a purposeful physical receiver while the playable campaign board is now a crisp election control room built around the map and results.
Shared broadcast and editorial treatments unify campaign resources, action planning, state reports, decisions, recaps, forecasts, settings, and election night.
The production UI no longer relies on modern gradients, colored glows, pill-heavy cards, decorative hover motion, gameplay blur, or anachronistic web fonts.
A ninth Chromium journey protects the design tokens, sharp candidate cards, masthead language, wire label, and unfiltered strategy interface.

title: First-party audio only
notes: Removed the third-party music account connection, OAuth flow, playback API calls, settings controls, title-screen card, and election-night autoplay behavior.
Returning players now have any legacy music authorization token, state, and verifier removed from local browser storage.
Deleted the unused weekly streaming-track data and integration-specific interface styles from the production source.
Added browser coverage proving that no connection controls remain and legacy authorization state is cleared.

title: Flagship launch and contributor foundation
notes: The opening board now follows the certified 1976 state-winner map instead of arbitrary randomized starting support.
A typed, validated scenario registry and documented historical example give contributors a stable content boundary outside GameEngine.
The title screen, campaign engine, and strategy interface now load in separate production chunks for a faster playable homepage.
GitHub Pages deployment, launch screenshots, contributor guidance, issue templates, dependency upgrades, and repository cleanup make the project ready for public collaboration.
The quality gate now covers 31 deterministic and unit tests plus seven Chromium journeys, including a complete 25-week campaign.

title: Accessible strategy board and full-campaign quality gate
notes: A keyboard-operable state table and responsive layout make the campaign board usable beyond the color map and desktop viewport.
Reduced motion and CRT visual effects are persisted, system-aware settings with global behavior and accessible dialog controls.
Seven Playwright journeys cover setup, weekly resolution, autosave, accessibility, mobile play, and a complete 25-week campaign through all 538 EV.
GitHub Actions now gates releases on version verification, lint, 26 unit tests, production build, and browser tests.

title: Campaign continuity and election night
notes: Campaigns autosave locally and resume with exact deterministic simulation continuity.
Election night now resolves all 538 EV from live state probabilities and reveals calls through an accessible election desk.
The title screen no longer interrupts first-time play with a Spotify prompt and now explains candidate and difficulty asymmetry.
The 25-test suite covers save validation, RNG restoration, insolvency safety, full election resolution, and deterministic final results.

title: Historical campaign decisions and the road to 270
notes: Every campaign week now presents a sourced 1976 decision with visible costs and tradeoffs.
The campaign desk identifies expected EV, battlegrounds, must-holds, best flips, and routes to 270.
Weekly recaps explain electoral movement, cash flow, resolved actions, and the biggest state shifts.
Automated coverage now validates the full event timeline, all debate weeks, deterministic resolution, and road-to-270 planning.

title: Deterministic campaign foundation
notes: Weekly actions now resolve together without remove-action side effects.
Campaigns use seeded simulation randomness and probability-based forecast helpers.
The opponent obeys the shared six-action ceiling and Maine restores the 538-EV total.
Vitest now covers replay, planning purity, action legality, and forecast invariants.
